nodes.label: Testing Frontier LLMs' Physics Literacy in Parallel Physical Worlds
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Introduces four-stage diagnostic for evaluating LLM physics reasoning: induction, formulation, prediction, review

nodes.label: Four-Stage Physics Reasoning Diagnostic
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Decomposes physics understanding into four independent cognitive moves: induction, formulation, prediction, review; operationalizes Whewell's and Hempel's scientific method tradition

nodes.label: Parallel Physics Worlds Framework
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Counterfactual physics frameworks designed to separate genuine reasoning from training-data memorization; three worlds: F=mv, Aristotelian mechanics, Decay World

nodes.label: Induction: Extract Regularity from Observations
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: First cognitive move: extract from theoretically uninterpreted observations a regularity explaining all of them; exemplified by Maxwell's unification of electric and magnetic phenomena

nodes.label: Formulation: Rewrite into Operational Form
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Second cognitive move: rewrite induced regularity into operational form applicable by third party; exemplified by Maxwell's four equations and displacement current addition

nodes.label: Prediction: Make Quantitatively Checkable Predictions
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Third cognitive move: use operational form to make quantitatively checkable predictions about new situations; exemplified by Maxwell's prediction of electromagnetic waves

nodes.label: Review: Identify Errors and Boundaries
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Fourth cognitive move: identify which step might be wrong, which boundary uncovered, which mechanism unexplained; exemplified by Maxwell's equations revealing seed of special relativity

nodes.label: Qualitative-Versus-Quantitative Asymmetry in Physics Reasoning
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Empirical pattern: models almost never predict wrong direction of change but frequently compute wrong ratio by slipping back to standard-physics relations

nodes.label: LLM Judge Reliability Transfer Problem
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Methodology finding: LLM judge reliability does not transfer across frameworks; self-review weak in every framework

nodes.label: Self-Review Weakness in LLM Physics Reasoning
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Stage 4 self-review is weak in every framework; model's own review wrongly reports no earlier error in at least two-thirds of trials that actually contained one

nodes.label: Reasoning Versus Memorization in LLMs
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Central debate: whether LLMs perform genuine reasoning or template retrieval from training data; counterfactual frameworks designed to separate these

nodes.label: World Modeling as Necessary but Insufficient for Physics Understanding
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Model without internal representation cannot produce independently checkable formal theory; having representation does not mean it can write theory down

nodes.label: Accuracy as Insufficient Evaluation Metric
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Accuracy cannot distinguish physics understanding from prior exposure; carries no information about cognitive boundary; does not reveal where reasoning breaks down

nodes.label: Three Levels of AI Autonomy in Science
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Low autonomy: execution within established theory; Medium autonomy: hypothesis generation; High autonomy: solving precisely stated problem; all remain anchored to human-supplied framework

nodes.label: Complete Scientific Theory Construction
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Requires starting from theoretically uninterpreted observations, independently inducing theoretical system, making quantifiable predictions; no AI system has independently completed this

nodes.label: Whewell-Hempel Scientific Method Tradition
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Older tradition of scientific method: induction, colligation, prediction, consilience; describes working path in routine physics, not revolutionary moments

nodes.label: Counterfactual Task Variants for Separating Reasoning from Recitation
nodes.author: Dong Zhang
nodes.rationale: Broader observation that counterfactual variants can separate reasoning from recitation; model cannot have seen standard answer during training

nodes.label: Four-Stage Protocol for Testing LLM Physics Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Proposes a four-stage protocol (induction, formulation, prediction, review) to isolate and test distinct cognitive capabilities in LLM physics reasoning, avoiding confounds from end-to-end testing.

nodes.label: Stage 1: Induction
nodes.rationale: Model receives observation set and must induce rules explaining phenomena without being given the rule explicitly.

nodes.label: Stage 2: Formulation
nodes.rationale: Model rewrites Stage 1 rules into operational form with explicit definitions, scopes, and boundary cases.

nodes.label: Stage 3: Prediction
nodes.rationale: Model applies Stage 2 operational rules to generate quantitative predictions on unseen scenarios.

nodes.label: Stage 4: Review
nodes.rationale: Model performs self-assessment on its own Stages 1–3 outputs to identify errors; reported separately as metacognitive axis, not in composite gate.

nodes.label: F=mv Counterfactual World (Easy)
nodes.rationale: Single-equation counterfactual replacing F=ma with F=mv; shallowest difficulty level testing induction and rule organization.

nodes.label: Aristotelian Mechanics (Medium)
nodes.rationale: Historically real framework with multi-principle structure; tests ability to suspend training-data prior that labels Aristotelian as wrong.

nodes.label: Decay World (Hard)
nodes.rationale: Multi-domain counterfactual with no underlying substrate; 1% per-second decay across mechanical, thermal, rotational, orbital domains tests cross-domain unification and quantitative computation.

nodes.label: Claude Opus 4.7
nodes.rationale: Frontier LLM tested across all three frameworks; version string pinned per round.

nodes.label: GPT-5.5
nodes.rationale: Frontier LLM tested across all three frameworks; version string pinned per round.

nodes.label: Gemini 3.1 Pro
nodes.rationale: Frontier LLM tested across all three frameworks; version string pinned per round; tested but not used as judge.

nodes.label: Irreversible Pre-Registration
nodes.rationale: SHA-256-sealed evaluation specification locked before production data generation; prevents post-hoc criterion drift through git-enforced immutability.

nodes.label: Dual LLM Judges with Human Audit
nodes.rationale: Every stage output judged independently by Claude and GPT; disagreement rate >25% triggers human audit; canonical verdict replaces LLM verdicts for disputed cases.

nodes.label: Composite Verdict Definition
nodes.rationale: Trial passes only if Stage 1, Stage 2, and all Stage 3 scenarios pass on content axis; structural axis joins conjunction where applicable; Stage 4 reported separately as metacognitive axis.

nodes.label: Bottleneck Migration Across Difficulty Gradient
nodes.rationale: Empirical signature of difficulty gradient: failures concentrate in different cognitive moves across frameworks. F=mv shows per-model heterogeneity; Aristotelian shows shared Stage 1 training-prior bottleneck; Decay shows Stage 3 quantitative-computation bottleneck.

nodes.label: Qualitative Direction vs Quantitative Ratio Asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Across 105 quantitative predictions (45 at F=mv, 60 at Decay): 0 direction-wrong predictions but 23 of 60 ratio-leaked at Decay. Models know sign of change but cannot compute ratio under cross-domain pressure.

nodes.label: Stage 4 Over-Claim Consistently High
nodes.rationale: Over-claim rate 67–83% across all three frameworks on failure-containing trials; no reliable improvement on harder frameworks; contradicts 'models know what they don't know' calibration framing.

nodes.label: Judge Reliability Does Not Transfer Across Frameworks
nodes.rationale: More reliable judge reverses between frameworks: OpenAI 82% on Aristotelian, Claude 83% on F=mv, Claude 67% on Decay. Single-judge evaluation unsafe; dual-judge plus disagreement-rate plus audit necessary.

nodes.label: Reproducible LLM-Judge Fabrication Failure
nodes.rationale: OpenAI judge on Decay World slides from literal substring matching to semantic association in banned-token test; fabricates citations (16 of 18 disagreement verdicts defective); triggered by long ban list and high topical overlap.

nodes.label: Induction Is Framework-Specific, Not Stable Model Property
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 pass rates swing widely across frameworks; bottleneck differs: F=mv (reimporting F=ma), Aristotelian (training-prior suppression), Decay (universality across domains).

nodes.label: Rule-Set Organization Is Prompt-Responsive
nodes.rationale: Structural axis major differentiator at F=mv; axiomatization cue doubled structural pass rate at F=mv and saturated at Aristotelian; capability present but not exhibited by default.

nodes.label: N=5 Trials Per Model Per Framework
nodes.rationale: Descriptive, not statistical inference; per-model composite counts too thin for confidence-level claims; findings about patterns in 45 trials, not population inference.

nodes.label: Three Frameworks Do Not Span Difficulty Gradient
nodes.rationale: One Easy, one Medium, one Hard; no multiple frameworks at single difficulty level; bottleneck-migration claim consistent with three data points but not directly tested.

nodes.label: Three Frontier Models Not Exhaustive
nodes.rationale: Claims apply to Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro at pinned versions; reasoning-trained or physics-fine-tuned models could differ; no open-weight models tested.

nodes.label: Composite PASS Rate Insufficient for Cognitive Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Identical composite PASS (6/15) at F=mv and Aristotelian masks completely different cognitive pictures; per-stage decomposition necessary to isolate which move failed.

nodes.label: Judging Infrastructure Is Part of Experimental Design
nodes.rationale: Pre-registration floor not ceiling; audit pathway triggered by disagreement threshold necessary at scale; single-judge design would produce systematically wrong verdicts on at least one framework.

nodes.label: Framework Choice Is Most Important Benchmark-Design Decision
nodes.rationale: Counterfactual frameworks separate reasoning from recitation; multi-domain counterfactual with no substrate probes capabilities single-equation and historical frameworks do not; bottleneck migration more informative than pass-rate ordering.

nodes.label: Content Axis Criteria N1–N6 for F=mv
nodes.rationale: Six necessary conditions on induced rules: present-push principle (N1), proportionalities (N2–N3), no-build-up signature (N4), unified-fall picture (N5), push combination (N6); failing any one is Stage 1 FAIL.

nodes.label: Structural Axis Criteria N9–N12
nodes.rationale: Four conditions on rule-set organization: parsimony (rule count), independence (no paraphrase), traceability (maps to observations), hierarchy (cross-references for 5+ rules).

nodes.label: Content Axis Criteria N1–N8 for Aristotelian
nodes.rationale: Eight necessary conditions: two-regime distinction (N1), heavier-falls-faster (N2), medium-resistance (N3), shape dependence (N4), directional preference (N5), heaven/earth split (N6), projectile tension (N7), floating account (N8).

nodes.label: Content Axis Criteria N1–N6 for Decay World
nodes.rationale: Six necessary conditions: closed-system loss (N1), multiplicative decline (N2), time-fixed rate (N3), universality across domains (N4), independence from material (N5), numerical rate ~0.99/s (N6).

nodes.label: F=mv Composite PASS: 6 of 15
nodes.rationale: Claude 3/5, GPT 2/5, Gemini 1/5; failures concentrated on different cognitive moves per model.

nodes.label: Aristotelian Composite PASS: 6 of 15
nodes.rationale: Claude 2/5, GPT 4/5, Gemini 0/5; structural axis uniformly passed; failures driven by Stage 1 training-prior suppression.

nodes.label: Decay World Composite PASS: 0 of 15
nodes.rationale: All trials fail by Stage 3; 14 of 15 fail Stage 3 check itself; qualitative direction perfect (0 wrong), quantitative ratio leaked 23 of 60 times.

nodes.label: Axiomatization Prompt Cue
nodes.rationale: Paragraph asking for smallest rule set with explicit cross-references; lifted composite PASS and reduced structural failures at F=mv and Aristotelian; did not rescue Decay content axis.

nodes.label: Banned-Word List for F=mv
nodes.rationale: 8 tokens: velocity, acceleration, momentum, mass, inertia, gravity, friction, energy, F=ma, physicist names; prevents importing answer through memorized vocabulary.

nodes.label: Banned-Word List for Aristotelian
nodes.rationale: 11 tokens: inertia, acceleration, force, momentum, energy, mass, density, gravity, vacuum, friction, post-Aristotelian physicist names; prevents Newtonian category import.

nodes.label: Banned-Word List for Decay World
nodes.rationale: 20+ tokens across three layers: energy-thermodynamics (energy, kinetic, potential, conservation, entropy, Hamiltonian, Lagrangian), decay-mechanism (friction, drag, damping, dissipation, viscous, air resistance, attenuation), mechanics (force, mass, acceleration, momentum, inertia), physicist names.

nodes.label: Stage Isolation Design
nodes.rationale: Each stage runs in fresh API session with new client and session UUID; cross-stage context reuse forbidden; Stage k+1 receives only final response text of Stage k, not chain-of-thought or intermediate state.

nodes.label: Temperature Zero Request
nodes.rationale: Protocol requests temperature 0 where provider exposes parameter; runner records requested value and uses provider default if not exposed.

nodes.label: Four Types of Newton Leak in Aristotelian
nodes.rationale: Banned-vocabulary derivatives, training-data concept import, standard-physics knowledge exposure, missing framework concept; lexical banned-token check alone insufficient; audit catches unmistakably Newtonian content.

nodes.label: Ratio Leak Mechanism in Decay World
nodes.rationale: Model correctly names per-second exponential decay but computes per-scenario number using standard-physics relation; treats unstated energy as underlying decaying quantity; back-derives measured quantity from it; gives inconsistent rate across domains.

nodes.label: Physics Reasoning Benchmark: Counterfactual Worlds
nodes.author: Unknown
nodes.rationale: Tests frontier LLMs on three physics frameworks with counterfactual rules to measure hypothetico-deductive reasoning across induction, formulation, prediction, and review stages.

nodes.label: F=mv Framework (Easy)
nodes.rationale: Single-equation counterfactual where pace is set by present push, not acceleration. Tests whether models can induce non-Newtonian mechanics from 12 observations.

nodes.label: Aristotelian Framework (Medium)
nodes.rationale: Historical physics framework where heavier bodies fall faster, motion requires sustained external cause. Tests induction of pre-Galilean mechanics.

nodes.label: Decay World Framework (Hard)
nodes.rationale: Four-domain counterfactual where all closed systems decay multiplicatively at ~0.99 per second, independent of material/weight. Designed to surface quantitative-computation bottleneck.

nodes.label: Four-Stage Hypothetico-Deductive Protocol
nodes.rationale: Decomposed cognitive chain: Stage 1 (induction from observations), Stage 2 (formulation as operational rules), Stage 3 (quantitative prediction), Stage 4 (self-review). Fresh API sessions between stages prevent context reuse.

nodes.label: Dual LLM Judge + Human Audit
nodes.rationale: Two independent LLM judges produce verdicts at each stage; human audit serves as canonical tie-breaker when inter-judge disagreement exceeds pre-registered threshold. Reveals judge-reliability asymmetries.

nodes.label: SHA-256 Pre-Registration Locks
nodes.rationale: Each framework's evaluation specification locked under git tag with SHA-256 hash in file header. CI check recomputes hash on every commit to prevent post-hoc modification.

nodes.label: Headline Composite PASS Rates
nodes.rationale: F=mv: 6/15, Aristotelian: 6/15, Decay World: 0/15 (content ∧ structural for first two; content only for Decay World). Same composite score masks different failure modes.

nodes.label: Qualitative Direction vs Quantitative Computation Asymmetry
nodes.rationale: Across 60 Stage 3 predictions at Decay World, no model predicted wrong sign of change, but 23/60 gave ratios derivable only from standard-physics relation, not framework rule. Failure mode the multi-domain framework was designed to surface.

nodes.label: Stage 4 Over-Claim Rate
nodes.rationale: Over-claim rate at or above two-thirds (67–83%) across all three frameworks. 'More reliable' LLM judge against human audit reverses between frameworks, suggesting frontier-model pattern.

nodes.label: Banned-Token Test
nodes.rationale: Lexical test banning modern-physics tokens (velocity, acceleration, inertia, momentum, mass, gravity, friction, energy, physicist names, F=ma). Decay World test surfaced reproducible failure mode in one judge with fabricated-citation form.

nodes.label: Benchmark Design Principle
nodes.rationale: Physics-reasoning benchmark should report which cognitive move failed, not aggregate accuracy. Two frameworks with same composite score but different failure stages carry more evaluation information than three accuracies dropping linearly.

nodes.label: Project Repository
nodes.rationale: All pre-registration files, raw prompts, model responses, dual-judge verdicts, human-audit records, framework artifacts, and reproducibility scripts released. Canonical reproducibility recipe in README.md.
